BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r2.claim: Qutil al-insan is a curse and rebuke, like saying may the person be ruined; it condemns a condition so vile that he scarcely deserves life.
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r2.anchor: “kutile” Türkçemizde “kahrolası” tâbiri gibi gazab ve zemme delâlet eyleyen beddua suretinde takbihten kinayedir

ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r3.claim: The exclamation about ingratitude states the reason for the rebuke: people forget their origin, gifts from the benefactor, and God's power despite reminders.
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r3.anchor: vücûdunun mebde’inden me‘âdı saatine kadar müstağrak olduğu nimeti unutmak ve mün‘imden ve onun kudretinden zühûl etmek

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r1.claim: After describing Quraysh leaders' pride over poor Muslims, Rāzī asks what warrants that pride when human life begins as a lowly drop and ends as a stinking corpse.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r1.anchor: فكأنه قيل : وأي سبب في هذا العجب والترفع مع أن أوله نطفة قذوة وآخره جيفة مذرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r2.claim: Human creation provides evidence both for a Creator and for resurrection, answering pride and disbelief alike.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r2.anchor: فإن خلقة الإنسان تصلح لأن يستدل بها على وجود الصانع ، ولأن يستدل بها على القول بالبعث

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r3.claim: Some commentators say this verse was revealed about ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون : نزلت الآية في عتبة بن أبي لهب

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r4.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r4.claim: Others identify the human as the people the Messenger attended while leaving Ibn Umm Maktūm.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون : المراد بالإنسان الذين أقبل الرسول عليهم وترك ابن أم مكتوم بسببهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r5.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes the target every rich person who looks down on the poor because of wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد ذم كل غني ترفع على فقير بسبب الغنى والفقر

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r6.claim: Rāzī prefers the general reading: the criticism's cause applies broadly, the later account of human origins is general, and this reading yields greater benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r6.anchor: والذي يدل على ذلك وجوه أحدها : أنه تعالى ذمهم لترفعهم فوجب أن يعم الحكم بسبب عموم العلة

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r7.claim: The opening is a curse, among the Arabs' harshest, and signals that the proud deserve the gravest punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r7.anchor: قوله تعالى : { قتل الإنسان } دعاء عليه وهي من أشنع دعواتهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r8.claim: The exclamation expresses astonishment at the extreme ingratitude that produces so many evils.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r8.anchor: وما أكفره تعجب من إفراطه في كفران نعمة الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r9.claim: Although curse and astonishment usually suit the powerless or uninformed, Rāzī explains them as familiar Arab speech conveying that these people deserve severe punishment for grave vice.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r9.anchor: أن ذلك ورد على أسلوب كلام العرب وتحقيقة ما ذكرنا أنه تعالى بين أنهم استحقوا أعظم أنواع العقاب

RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r10.claim: Rāzī frames the following account around human life's three stages: beginning, middle, and end.
RAZI-FULL:v31p54#3/r10.anchor: لكل محدث ثلاث مراتب أوله ووسطه وآخره

STUDYQURAN:80:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r1.claim: Qutila al-insan means may man perish.
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r1.anchor: May man perish translates qutila al-insān

STUDYQURAN:80:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r2.speaker: IK and Q
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r2.claim: IK and Q also render the phrase as may man be cursed.
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r2.anchor: could also be rendered, “May man be cursed” (IK, Q)

STUDYQURAN:80:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r3.claim: The phrase refers to deniers without an argument, who lack knowledge of the truth and think it far-fetched.
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r3.anchor: refer to those who deny the truth without any supporting argument, but only because they lack knowledge of it

STUDYQURAN:80:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r4.claim: Afkara indicates both ingratitude toward God and disbelief in God.
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r4.anchor: Ungrateful translates afkara, which indicates both ingratitude toward and disbelief in God

STUDYQURAN:80:17/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r5.claim: Q records readings that man is accursed for what he disbelieves, or asks what mankind disbelieves.
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r5.anchor: Thus this verse could also be read, “Man is accursed for what he disbelieves,” or “Mankind is accursed; for what does he disbelieve?” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:80:17/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r6.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r6.claim: Some say the verse concerns an individual who accepted Islam then apostatized when Sūrah 53 was revealed, and was cursed for rejecting the Quran after believing.
STUDYQURAN:80:17/r6.anchor: According to some, this verse relates to a specific individual who had accepted Islam, but apostatized when Sūrah 53 was revealed

TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r1.claim: Qutila al-insan means may the disbelieving human be cursed; the verse condemns his ingratitude.
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r1.anchor: ما كان في القرآن {قتل الإنسان} [عبس: 17] أو فعل بالإنسان

TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says Quranic wording that a human is killed or acted upon refers to the disbeliever.
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r2.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن مجاهد، قال: ما كان في القرآن {قتل الإنسان} [عبس: 17] أو فعل بالإنسان، فإنما عني به الكافر

TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r3.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r3.claim: Sufyan says he had heard that the person meant is the disbeliever.
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r3.anchor: عن سفيان، {قتل الإنسان ما أكفره} [عبس: 17] بلغني أنه الكافر

TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r4.claim: One reading takes the expression as exclamation: how astonishing his disbelief despite God's beneficence and favors toward him.
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r4.anchor: وفي قوله: {أكفره} [عبس: 17] وجهان. أحدهما: التعجب من كفره، مع إحسان الله إليه، وأياديه عنده

TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r5.claim: The other reading is an interrogative: what made him disbelieve, or what thing caused his disbelief?
TAB-FULL:v24p110#2/r5.anchor: والآخر: ما الذي أكفره، أي أي شيء أكفره؟

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.claim: The passage condemns human ingratitude and recalls that God creates, measures, guides, causes death, buries, and resurrects the human, who owns none of this governance.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r1.anchor: بيان دعاء على الانسان وتعجيب من مبالغته في الكفر بربوبية ربه وإشارة إلى أمره حدوثا وبقاء فإنه لا يملك لنفسه شيئا

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.claim: Even food alone displays God's vast, subtle governance and immeasurable mercy; overlooking this care and failing to give thanks is astonishing human injustice and ingratitude.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r2.anchor: ولو نظر الإنسان إلى طعامه فقط وهو مظهر واحد من مظاهر تدبيره وغرفة من بحار رحمته رأى من وسيع التدبير ولطيف الصنع

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.claim: These verses can continue the preceding passage as one context, although some commentators say they were revealed for a separate occasion discussed later.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r3.anchor: لا تأبى الاتصال بما قبلها سياقا واحدا وإن قال بعضهم أنها نزلت لسبب آخر كما سيجيء

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r4.claim: The opening is a curse upon the human for his natural tendency to follow desire, forget God's lordship, and arrogantly resist divine commands.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r4.anchor: دعاء على الإنسان لما أن في طبعه التوغل في اتباع الهوى ونسيان ربوبية ربه والاستكبار عن اتباع أوامره

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r5.claim: The phrase expresses amazement at extreme concealment of manifest truth: the human knows God governs him and that he has no independent control.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r5.anchor: تعجيب من مبالغة في الكفر وستر الحق الصريح وهو يرى أنه مدبر بتدبير الله

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r6.claim: Here kufr means covering truth generally, including denying God's lordship and abandoning worship; the context's account of divine governance supports this sense over mere ingratitude for blessings.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r6.anchor: فالمراد بالكفر مطلق ستر الحق وينطبق على إنكار الربوبية وترك العبادة ويؤيده ما في ذيل الآية

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r7.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf calls the opening a particularly severe curse and reads the following phrase as amazement at excessive ingratitude to God, emphasizing its harshness and concentrated blame.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r7.anchor: دعاء عليه وهي من أشنع دعواتهم لأن القتل قصارى شدائد الدنيا وفظائعها

TABATABAI:80:17-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r8.claim: An alternative parses the phrase as a question asking what made the human disbelieve; al-Tabataba'i judges the preceding exclamatory reading more eloquent.
TABATABAI:80:17-19/r8.anchor: استفهامية والمعنى ما هو الذي جعله كافرا، والوجه المتقدم أبلغ

BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r19.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r19.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r19.claim: The phrase is a curse against the human being, the most dreadful worldly calamity; construing killing as cursing denotes spiritual destruction, an even harsher punishment, and here the target is the unbeliever.
BURSEVI:v10p259#2/r19.anchor: {قتل الانسان} دعاء عليه بأشنع الدعوات فإن القتل غاية شدائد الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p260/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r1.claim: Mā akfarahu means how intense his disbelief and ingratitude are despite God's abundant beneficence.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r1.anchor: ما أشد كفره بالله مع كثرة إحسانه إليه

BURSEVI:v10p260/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r2.claim: The exclamation portrays excessive ingratitude; it is not literal divine surprise, since true surprise comes from ignorance of a cause, but a divine expression inviting people to marvel at his unbelief and recognize his deserving punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r2.anchor: تعجب من إفراطه في الكفران أي على صورته فإن حقيقة التعجب إنما تتصور

BURSEVI:v10p260/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r3.claim: Some say the unbeliever merits God's curse and magnified condemnation because he failed to know his Maker and himself, through whose knowledge he would know his Maker.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : لعن الله الكافر وعظم كفره حيث لم يعرف صانعه ولم يعرف

BURSEVI:v10p260/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r4.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p260/r4.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the Arabic curse and exclamation are rhetorical, not evidence of divine inability to avenge or ignorance; they express intense wrath and emphatic blame for a heinous deed.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ : هذا الدعاء وارد على أسلوب كلام العرب فهو ليس من قبيل دعاء

BURSEVI:v10p260/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r5.claim: Alternatively, mā akfarahu is a reproachful question asking what drove the person to disbelief.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما أكفره استفهاما بمعنى التقريع والتوبيخ

BURSEVI:v10p260/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p260/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p260/r6.claim: The human being may mean the self-satisfied person previously described, or humanity as a class including him and others.
BURSEVI:v10p260/r6.anchor: والمراد من الإنسان إما من استغنى عن القرآن المذكور نعوته وإما الجنس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reads “may the human be cursed” as a curse upon Utba.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r1.anchor: هو قال ابن عباس: لعن عتبة (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r2.claim: The exegetes say the verse was revealed about Utba ibn Abi Lahab.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت في (عتبة بن) (¬7) أبي لهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r3.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r3.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi gloss the question as “What made him disbelieve?”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬9)، الكلبي (¬10): ما الذي أكفره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r4.claim: Al-Farra says this is the established exegetical reading, while allowing an exclamative construction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r4.anchor: وقال (¬11) الفراء: بهذا الوجه جاء التفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives two construals: an exclamation inviting people to marvel at human disbelief, like 2:175, or a rebuking question, “What made him disbelieve?”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p221/r5.anchor: وشرح الزجاج القولين، فقال: يكون على جهة لفظ التعجب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r11.claim: “Qutila” is a curse against the unbeliever, identified as ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r11.anchor: { قتل الإنسان } لعن الكافر. يعني: عتبة بن أبي لهب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:6-18/r12.claim: The phrase means: how intense is his unbelief.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r1.claim: The denunciation does not target humanity generally; it addresses pagan opponents who disputed the Prophet and denied resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r1.anchor: Burada “Kahrolası o insan!” şeklindeki yergi ifadesiyle genel olarak insanlığın değil, Hz. Peygamber’le yaptıkları tartışmalarda yeniden dirilmeyi inkâr eden putperestlerin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r2.speaker: bir rivayete göre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r2.claim: One report identifies the particular person denounced as Utbah, the son of Abu Lahab.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r2.anchor: bir rivayete göre özellikle Ebû Leheb’in oğlu Utbe’nin kastedildiği

BURHAN:v4p403/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p403/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p403/r8.claim: The author classifies mā in the two Qur'anic exclamations as exclamatory; there is no third example except in Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's reading of 82:6.

BURHAN:v4p403/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p403/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p403/r10.claim: In exclamatory constructions mā is nominative as the subject, while the following clause is its predicate; exclamation and interrogation are closely related.
BURHAN:v4p403/r10.anchor: وتكون في موضع رفع بالابتداء وما خبر وهو قريب مما قبله لأن الاستفهام والتعجب بينهما تلازم

BURHAN:v2p318/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r1.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p318/r1.claim: One view disallows marveling at God's act, since saying how great God is might suggest that something made Him great, whereas His attributes are eternal.
BURHAN:v2p318/r1.anchor: لايتعجب من فعل الله فلا يقال ما أعظم الله

BURHAN:v2p318/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p318/r2.claim: Another view permits such language because magnifying God accords with worshippers' belief in His greatness and power; an anonymous poem says He can bring the distant near.
BURHAN:v2p318/r2.anchor: وقيل بجوازه باعتبار انه يحب تعظيم الله شيء من صفاته

BURHAN:v2p318/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
BURHAN:v2p318/r3.claim: Some scholars answer that astonishment magnifies the matter itself; it need not imply that another agent caused it, and its cause may simply be hidden from us.
BURHAN:v2p318/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين التعحب انما يقال لتعظيم الامر المتعجب منه

BURHAN:v2p318/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p318/r6.claim: The preferred view treats divine astonishment as directed toward the audience: God knows why people marvel, and His knowledge of what merits wonder is called wonder.
BURHAN:v2p318/r6.anchor: والمختار الاول وما وقع منه اول بالنظر إلى المخاطب أي علمت اسباب ما يتعجب منه العباد

BURHAN:v2p318/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p318/r7.claim: The dispute turns on whether true astonishment requires that the cause of the astonishing matter be hidden.
BURHAN:v2p318/r7.anchor: وأصل الخلاف في هذه المسالة يلتف على خلاف آخر وهو أن حقيقة التعجب

BURHAN:v2p318/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p318/r8.claim: The Qur'anic exclamation forms are limited to فما أصبرهم على النار, قتل الإنسان ما أكفره, and يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك in a reading that adds a hamza.
BURHAN:v2p318/r8.anchor: ولم يقع في القرآن صيغة التعجب الا

BURHAN:v2p318/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.speaker: المحققون
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.claim: The learned explain divine exclamation, prayer, and hope from the hearer's perspective; Sibawayh reads 20:44 as Moses and Aaron acting on their own hope, which Ibn al-Da'i praises.
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.anchor: ثم قال المحققون التعجب مصروف إلى المخاطب ولهذا تلطف الزمخشري

BURHAN:v3p221/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p221/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p221/r3.claim: The wording may match its meaning in measure; the author cites this verse as an example of that balanced form.
BURHAN:v3p221/r3.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قتل الإنسان ما أكفره ﴾ 2 وهو كثير

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r23.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r23.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r23.claim: The phrase means, “Cursed be man”: how great his disbelief is.

BURHAN:v4p57/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p57/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p57/r1.claim: The author classifies ‘cursed be man, how ungrateful he is’ as divine expression of wonder, alongside ‘how patient they are over the Fire’ and ‘how clearly He sees and hears.’
BURHAN:v4p57/r1.anchor: التعجب الواقع في كلام الله نحو

ITQAN:v2p512#4/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p512#4/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p512#4/r5.claim: Exclamatory mā occurs in two Qur’anic examples, including “How ungrateful man is”; grammatically it is a complete indefinite subject whose following clause is its predicate.
ITQAN:v2p512#4/r5.anchor: تعجبية نحو ﴿ فما أصبرهم على النار ﴾ ﴿ قتل الإنسان ما أكفره ﴾ ولا ثالث لهما في القرآن إلا في قراءة سعيد بن جبير

SULAMI:v2p373#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#6/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p373#6/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says ignorance in seeking guidance and complacency in what one's Lord promised block a person from the paths of good.
SULAMI:v2p373#6/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : منع الإنسان عن طريق الخيرات لجهله بطلب رشده وسكونه إلى ما وعد له ربه

SULAMI:v2p373#6/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#6/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p373#6/r2.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads the verse as exposing man's great ignorance of gnosis, which itself stems from his ignorance.
SULAMI:v2p373#6/r2.anchor: وقال الواسطي - رحمة الله عليه - : ما اجهله بالمعرفة وذلك لجهله

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r3.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r3.claim: Ikrima reports that the verse was revealed about ʿUtba ibn Abi Lahab, who said he disbelieved in the Lord of the Star.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ قتل الإنسان ما أكفره ﴾ قال نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب حين قال كفرت برب النجم

AKHFASH:v2p567/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p567/r3.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p567/r3.claim: One reported interpretation takes mā akfarahu as an exclamation: How ungrateful the human is.
AKHFASH:v2p567/r3.anchor: معناه على وجهين، قال بعضهم "على التعجب"

AKHFASH:v2p567/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p567/r4.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p567/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation takes mā akfarahu as a question meaning what made him disbelieve.

DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.claim: In the rebuke “Perish man,” al-insān means ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab; the same referent appears in the command to look at food.
DAMGHANI:v1p51/r3.anchor: الرابع عشر : الإنسان عتبة بن أبي لهب . قوله تعالى في سورة عبس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.claim: Qatl can be a curse or imprecation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.anchor: والثالث : اللعن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الذاريات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r2.claim: Mā can express exclamation, with an implied sense of “what” or “how.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r2.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى التعجب وتقديره أي شيء

FARRA:v3p236/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p236/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p236/r9.claim: ما أكفره can be an exclamation meaning how unbelieving he is.

FARRA:v3p236/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p236/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p236/r10.claim: It can instead ask what made him disbelieve; al-Farrāʾ says this is the interpretation transmitted in tafsir.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r1.claim: Curses such as قتل الخراصون, قتل الإنسان, and قاتلهم الله express blame, not a wish that the stated harm literally occur.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r1.anchor: كقول الله عز وجل: قتل الخراصون

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r3.claim: The same curse formulas can express amazement and praise at excellent speech, poetry, argument, or marksmanship rather than a literal wish of harm.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r3.anchor: قاتله الله ما أحسن ما قال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r4.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r4.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's archer poem says the man is not counted among his people, an exaggerated way of saying may God kill him for his astonishing shot.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r4.anchor: امرئ القيس في وصف رام أصاب : فهو لا تنمي رميته

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r5.speaker: كعب بن سعد الغنوي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r5.claim: Kaʿb b. Saʿd al-Ghanawi's هوت أمه is another conventional imprecation; the poet marvels at the man's extraordinary journeys.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r5.anchor: كعب بن سعد الغنوي : هوت أمه ما يبعث الصبح

NAHHAS:v5p151/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r1.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p151/r1.claim: Mujahid says that when God says a person was killed or acted upon, he means the unbeliever.
NAHHAS:v5p151/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد إذا قال الله تعالى قتل الإنسان أو فعل به فهو الكافر

NAHHAS:v5p151/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p151/r2.claim: قتل can mean “destroyed,” since the one killed has been destroyed; another reported gloss is “cursed.”
NAHHAS:v5p151/r2.anchor: ومعنى قتل أهلك لأن المقتول مهلك وقيل قتل لعن

NAHHAS:v5p151/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p151/r3.claim: He prefers reading ما as an interrogative: what made the person so unbelieving despite God’s signs and blessings? An alternative is an exclamation.
NAHHAS:v5p151/r3.anchor: الأولى أن تكون ما استفهاما أي ما الذي أكفره مع ظهور آيات الله جل وعز وأنعامه عليه وقيل هو تعجب

SAMIN-DURR:80:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:17/r1.claim: ما أكفره may be an exclamatory construction or an interrogative expressing astonishment.
SAMIN-DURR:80:17/r1.anchor: قوله: { مآ أكفره }: إما تعجب، وإما استفهام تعجب

ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r2.claim: The wording may express wonder at human disbelief, inviting the audience to marvel at it, like the wonder expressed in 2:175.
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r2.anchor: أي اعجبوا أنتم من كفر الإنسان

ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is a rebuke phrased as a question: “How ungrateful he is!”
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r3.anchor: ويجوز على معنى التوبيخ ولفظه لفظ الاستفهام.

ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n5/r1.claim: Asad reads qutila here as man's self-destruction and points readers to his note 9 on sūra 74 for this rendering.
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n5/r1.anchor: For my rendering of qutila as "he destroys himself", see surah 74, note 9.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p385/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p385/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p385/r1.claim: In Quranic passages using qutila against wrongdoers, the word is a curse or imprecation against them.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p385/r1.anchor: والقتل في هذه الآيات، دعاء عليهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r14.claim: The passage is said to concern ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab, who became Muslim after angering his father, then accepted money and went to Syria after declaring disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r14.anchor: قيل: نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب، غاضب أباه فأسلم، ثم استصلحه أبوه وأعطاه مالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r15.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that God send His dog against ʿUtba; a lion later killed him on the Syrian journey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r15.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «اللهم ابعث عليه كلبك يأكله»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r16.claim: Although the verse may have a specific occasion, الإنسان denotes disbelievers generally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r16.anchor: والآية، وإن نزلت في مخصوص، فالإنسان يراد به الكافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r17.claim: قتل is a curse or prayer against the person; killing is among the gravest worldly hardships.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r17.anchor: وقتل دعاء عليه، والقتل أعظم شدائد الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r18.claim: The apparent reading expresses amazement at extreme disbelief from the human point of view, since such amazement cannot apply to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r18.anchor: ما أكفره، الظاهر أنه تعجب من إفراط كفره، والتعجب بالنسبة للمخلوقين، إذ هو مستحيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r19.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r19.claim: Alternatively it is a reproachful question: what made him disbelieve, or what permits him to do so?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p408/r19.anchor: وقيل: ما استفهام توقيف، أي: أي شيء أكفره؟ أي جعله كافرا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r1.claim: Qutila is a curse in the harshest form; ma akfarahu exclaims at the extreme of human ingratitude and shows why the curse is deserved.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r1.anchor: دعاء عليه بأشنع الدعوات وأفظعها ما أكفره تعجيب من إفراطه في الكفران وبيان لاستحقاقه الدعاء عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r2.claim: The referent may be the person who considers himself independent of the Qur’an, or humankind generally; Alusi favors the general sense in view of the reported occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r2.anchor: والمراد به إما من استغنى عن القرآن الكريم الذي ذكزت نعوته الجليلة الموجبة للأقبال عليه والإيمان به وإما الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r3.claim: Ikrima’s occasion report identifies ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab: after becoming Muslim, he was reclaimed by his father, sent toward Syria, and announced disbelief in the Lord of the setting star. The Prophet prayed that God send a dog against him; a lion killed him on the journey despite his companions’ precautions, and his father mourned the fulfillment of the prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r3.anchor: الآية نزلت على ما أخرج ابن المنذر عن عكرمة في عتبة بن أبي لهب غاضب أباه فأسلم ثم استصلحه أبوه وأعطاه مالا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r4.speaker: جار الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r4.claim: Jār Allāh calls this one of the harshest, most concise expressions of anger: it combines a curse and an exclamation, understood figuratively for God and as eliciting wonder in listeners.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r4.anchor: قال جار الله لا ترى أسلوبا أغلظ منه ولا أدل على سخط ولا أبعد شوطا في المذمة مع تقارب طرفيه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r5.claim: The Imam says the first clause signals the gravest punishment by customary standards, and the second the gravest moral offenses; such wording was not heard before the Qur’an.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام أن الجملة الولى تدل على استحقاقهم أعظم أنواع العقاب عرفا والثانية تنبيه على أنهم اتصفوا بأعظم أنواع القبائح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r6.claim: Alusi says the couplet attributed to Imruʾ al-Qays about wishing for summer in winter and rejecting it when it comes is fabricated by a later poet, not pre-Islamic.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r6.anchor: وما نسب إلى امريء القيس من قوله يتمنى المرء في الصيف الشتا فإذا جاء الشتا أنكره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r7.claim: Alusi rejects the proposal that this predicts the killing of disbelievers through the later fighting verse, using past tense for certainty.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r7.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون قوله تعالى قتل الإنسان خبرا عن أنه سيقتل الكفار بإنزال آية القتال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r8.claim: He also rejects treating ما as interrogative, ‘What made him disbelieve?’ with the implied answer that nothing could justify his unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p43#2/r8.anchor: ونحوه ما قيل أن ما استفهامية أي أي شيء أكفره أي جعله كافرا بمعنى لا شيء يسوع له أن يكفر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r6.claim: The phrase curses the disbelieving human.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {قتل الإنسان} أي لعن الكافر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r7.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r7.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Utbah ibn Abi Lahab.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب (2)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r8.claim: The phrase marvels at the person's severe ingratitude to God despite His abundant beneficence and favors; al-Zajjaj says it means, Be astonished at his disbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r8.anchor: ما أشد كفره بالله مع كثرة إحسانه إليه وأياديه عنده، على طريق التعجب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r9.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil take mā as an interrogative: What made him disbelieve?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r9.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: هو "ما" الاستفهام، يعني: أي شيء حمله على الكفر؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r3.claim: This curses humanity in the harshest terms and expresses astonishment at its extreme ingratitude; its brevity conveys intense anger and blame.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r3.anchor: دعاه عليه بأشنع الدعوات وتعجب من إفراطه في الكفران

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r1.claim: After extolling the noble scribes and the exalted reminder they carry, the text turns to denounce those who refuse it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r1.anchor: ولما كان الوصف بهذه الأوصاف العالية للكتبة الذين أيديهم ظرف للصحف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r2.claim: The declarative curse that the human be killed is more forceful than an imperative curse.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r2.anchor: داعيا بأعظم شدائد الدنيا التي هي القتل في صيغة الخبر لأنه أبلغ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r3.claim: The human type forgets its Lord, exalts itself, and admires features fashioned by its Creator; it is readily corrupted and cursed unless God protects it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r3.anchor: هذا النوع الآنس بنفسه الناسي لربه المتكبر على غيره المعجب بشمائله التي أبدعها له خالقه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r4.claim: The phrase expresses astonishment and condemnation at covering up truth, denying resurrection, associating others with God, and resisting the evident proofs and merits of the Qurʾān.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r4.anchor: أي ما أشد تغطيته للحق وجحده له وعناده فيه لإنكاره البعث وإشراكه بربه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r5.claim: Though brief, the curse conveys immense anger and severe blame, and its lesson applies generally to everyone ungrateful for God’s blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r5.anchor: وهذا الدعاء على وجازته يدل على سخط عظيم وذم بليغ وهو وإن كان في مخصوص فالعبرة بعمومه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r6.claim: A report says the verse concerned ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab, who converted, then was induced by his father with money and a Syrian journey to renounce Islam and send a blasphemous message to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r6.anchor: روي أنها نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب غاضب أباه فأسلم ثم استصحله أبوه وأعطاء مالا وجهزه إلى الشام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r7.claim: When ʿUtba sent his denial, the Prophet prayed that God set one of His dogs upon him; a lion later reached the caravan and tore him apart.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p327/r7.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( اللهم أبعث عليه كلبا من كلابك ) فلما انتهى إلى مكان من الطريق فيه الأسد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r1.speaker: أبو لهب
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r1.claim: After the lion killed his son, the father acknowledged that whatever Muḥammad said came to pass, but that recognition did not benefit him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r1.anchor: وقال : ما قال محمد شيئا إلا كان , ومع ذلك فما نفعه ما عرف من ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r2.claim: God controls hearts, guiding whom He wills and leading astray whom He wills; both outcomes testify that all praise belongs to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r2.anchor: فسبحان من بيده القلوب يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r8.claim: Ikrima says the verse concerned ʿUtba ibn Abi Lahab, who declared disbelief in the Lord of the setting star; a lion seized him on the Syrian road after the Prophet prayed against him.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r8.anchor: قال: نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب حين قال: كفرت برب النجم إذا هوى

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r9.claim: Mujahid says that wherever the Qurʾan says “killed man,” it refers to an unbeliever.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن مجاهد قال: ما كان في القرآن قتل الإنسان إنما عني به الكافر

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the phrase as how extreme the disbelief is.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج {ما أكفره} قال: ما أشد كفره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r1.claim: The generic ‘human’ includes the self-sufficient man described earlier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r1.anchor: والذي عرف بقوله : { من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) يشمله العموم الذي أفاده تعريف { الإنسان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r2.claim: The expression began as a curse; early exegetes took it to mean ‘may he be cursed,’ as transmitted by al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās and said by Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Abū Mālik.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r2.anchor: والمفسرون الأولون جعلوا : { قتل الإنسان } أنه لعن ، رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس وقاله مجاهد وقتادة وأبو مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r3.speaker: الزمخشري في الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r3.claim: Al-Kashshāf calls it a curse directed against the person and one of the harshest curses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r3.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( دعاء عليه وهذا من أشنع دعواتهم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr distinguishes this from ‘God fight them’ and colloquial ‘God fight so-and-so,’ which express amazement; no such reading is needed because ‘how ungrateful he is’ already conveys it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r4.anchor: وهذا أمر مرجعه للاستعمال ولا داعي إلى حمله على التعجيب لأن قوله : { ما أكفره } يغني عن ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r5.claim: God’s imprecation of evil functions as disparagement and threat; a literal request is incompatible with divinity because people direct supplication to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r5.anchor: والدعاء بالسوء من الله تعالى مستعمل في التحقير والتهديد لظهور أن حقيقة الدعاء لا تناسب الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r6.claim: The passive follows from using the verb as a curse, where no actual killer matters; the Qur’an often uses this construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r6.anchor: وبناء { قتل } للمجهول متفرع على استعماله في الدعاء ، إذ لا غرض في قاتل يقتله ، وكثر في القرآن مبنيا للمجهول نحو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r7.claim: Definiteness may be generic and truly comprehensive, applying to every member of humankind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r7.anchor: وتعريف { الإنسان } يجوز أن يكون التعريف المسمى تعريف الجنس فيفيد استغراق جميع أفراد الجنس ، وهو استغراق حقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r8.claim: Alternatively, generic definiteness can express customary generalization over most people; the following description points to polytheists who denied resurrection, as most Arabs then did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r8.anchor: وقد يراد به استغراق معظم الأفراد بحسب القرائن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r9.claim: Mujāhid says every Qur’anic instance of ‘may the human be killed’ refers to an unbeliever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد : ما كان في القرآن { قتل الإنسان } فإنما عني به الكافر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r10.claim: Judgments about human kinds apply typically, not necessarily to every individual or at every moment; the clause marvels at the human kind’s unbelief or its intensity, though a few are not unbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p120/r10.anchor: فلا يقتضي اتصاف جميع الأفراد به ، بل قد يخلو عنه بعض الأفراد وقد يخلو عنه المتصف به في بعض الأحيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r1.claim: The generic ‘human’ resolves to unbelievers, who predominate in the species; disbelief has been widespread through history, including worship of powerless stone and wood or denial of a creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r1.anchor: فآل معنى الإنسان إلى الكفار من هذا الجنس وهم الغالب على نوع الإنسان .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r2.claim: One personal identification is Umayya ibn Khalaf, present when Ibn Umm Maktūm approached.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r2.anchor: فقيل : أريد به أمية بن خلف ، وكان ممن حواه المجلس الذي غشيه ابن أم مكتوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r3.claim: Among individual identifications, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r3.anchor: وعندي أن الأولى أن يكون أراد به الوليد بن المغيرة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab and relates a story unrelated to Ibn Umm Maktūm’s visit; Ibn ʿĀshūr treats the sentence as a new opening with an evident contextual connection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المراد عتبة بن أبي لهب ، وذكر في ذلك قصة لا علاقة لها بخبر المجلس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r5.claim: ‘How ungrateful he is’ explains the curse as contempt and threat, and expresses astonishment at this person’s severe unbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r5.anchor: وجملة { ما أكفره } تعليل لإنشاء الدعاء عليه دعاء التحقير والتهديد . وهذا تعجيب من شدة كفر هذا الإنسان .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r6.claim: The unbelief is severe in scope and intensity: it rejects God’s oneness, bodily resurrection, the Messenger, and revelation; it is firm and persists despite repeated reminders, warnings, and threats.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r6.anchor: ومعنى شدة الكفر أن كفره شديد كما وكيفا ، ومتى ، لأنه كفر بوحدانية الله ، وبقدرته على إعادة خلق الأجسام بعد الفناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r7.claim: This concise, forceful utterance conveys divine anger and blame with unmatched eloquence, and is one of the Qur’an’s comprehensive expressions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r7.anchor: وهذه الجملة بلغت نهاية الإيجاز وأرفع الجزالة بأسلوب غليظ دال على السخط بالغ حد المذمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r8.claim: The object of akfarahu is omitted because it is clear from the verb: ‘How ungrateful he is toward God!’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r8.anchor: وحذف المتعلق بلفظ { أكفره } لظهوره من لفظ ( أكفر ) وتقديره : ما أكفره بالله .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r9.claim: The phrase has metrical balance in ramal, in its first, truncated form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p121/r9.anchor: وفي قوله : { قتل الإنسان ما أكفره } محسن الاتزان فإنه من بحر الرمل من عروضه الأولى المحذوفة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r1.claim: The broad designation “the human” includes the self-sufficient person mentioned earlier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r1.anchor: والذي عرف بقوله : { من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) يشمله العموم الذي أفاده تعريف { الإنسان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r2.claim: The expression “may he be killed” originally functioned as an invocation calling death upon someone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r2.anchor: وفعل قتل فلان أصله دعاء عليه بالقتل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Abū Mālik also say that the phrase means the human was cursed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r3.anchor: والمفسرون الأولون جعلوا : { قتل الإنسان } أنه لعن ، رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس وقاله مجاهد وقتادة وأبو مالك .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf calls it an invocation against the person and one of the harshest such expressions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r4.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( دعاء عليه وهذا من أشنع دعواتهم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r5.claim: This differs from “May God fight them” or “May God fight so-and-so,” which express astonishment; no astonishment sense is needed here because the next phrase already conveys it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r5.anchor: أي فمورده غير مورد قوله تعالى : { قاتلهم الله } ( التوبة : 30 ) وقولهم : قاتل الله فلانا يريدون التعجب من حاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r6.claim: When God uses an evil invocation, it conveys contempt and threat, since literal supplication is unfitting: people direct their prayers to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r6.anchor: والدعاء بالسوء من الله تعالى مستعمل في التحقير والتهديد لظهور أن حقيقة الدعاء لا تناسب الإلاهية لأن الله هو الذي يتوجه إليه الناس بالدعاء .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r7.claim: The passive form follows from its use as an invocation, which has no intended killer; the Qur’an often uses this verb passively, as at 74:19.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r7.anchor: وبناء { قتل } للمجهول متفرع على استعماله في الدعاء ، إذ لا غرض في قاتل يقتله ، وكثر في القرآن مبنيا للمجهول نحو { فقتل كيف قدر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r8.claim: The definite noun may denote the entire human kind literally, or conventionally denote most people; the context points to polytheists who denied resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r8.anchor: وتعريف { الإنسان } يجوز أن يكون التعريف المسمى تعريف الجنس فيفيد استغراق جميع أفراد الجنس ، وهو استغراق حقيقي ، وقد يراد به استغراق معظم الأفراد بحسب القرائن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r9.speaker: جملة المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r9.claim: Most commentators take “the human” to mean the polytheists who denied resurrection, since most Arabs of that time rejected it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r9.anchor: وعلى ذلك جملة المفسرين ، فإن معظم العرب يومئذ كافرون بالبعث .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r10.claim: Mujāhid says every Qur’anic occurrence of “may the human be killed” refers to a disbeliever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد : ما كان في القرآن { قتل الإنسان } فإنما عني به الكافر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r11.claim: Judgments about a human kind generally describe what is prevalent, not every individual or every moment; the phrase marvels at humanity’s unbelief or its severity, though some humans do not disbelieve.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#18/r11.anchor: فلا يقتضي اتصاف جميع الأفراد به ، بل قد يخلو عنه بعض الأفراد وقد يخلو عنه المتصف به في بعض الأحيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r1.claim: Humanity has largely disbelieved in God throughout history, defended disbelief, worshipped powerless stone and wood, or denied having a creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r1.anchor: فغالب الناس كفروا بالله من أقدم عصور التاريخ وتفشى الكفر بين أفراد الإنسان وانتصروا له وناضلوا عنه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r2.claim: One reported identification takes the human to be Umayya ibn Khalaf, who was among those present when Ibn Umm Maktūm approached.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r2.anchor: فقيل : أريد به أمية بن خلف ، وكان ممن حواه المجلس الذي غشيه ابن أم مكتوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra as the specific person intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r3.anchor: وعندي أن الأولى أن يكون أراد به الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person as ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab; the story is unrelated to Ibn Umm Maktūm’s visit, so the sentence begins a new passage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المراد عتبة بن أبي لهب ، وذكر في ذلك قصة لا علاقة لها بخبر المجلس الذي غشيه ابن أم مكتوم ، فتكون الجملة مستأنفة استئنافا ابتدائيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r5.claim: The clause explains the curse as a threat and contempt, and marvels at the particular person’s extreme disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r5.anchor: وجملة { ما أكفره } تعليل لإنشاء الدعاء عليه دعاء التحقير والتهديد . وهذا تعجيب من شدة كفر هذا الإنسان .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r6.claim: His disbelief is extreme in scope, duration, and strength: he denies divine oneness, resurrection, prophethood, and revelation, persisting despite repeated warnings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r6.anchor: ومعنى شدة الكفر أن كفره شديد كما وكيفا ، ومتى ، لأنه كفر بوحدانية الله ، وبقدرته على إعادة خلق الأجسام بعد الفناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r7.claim: The compact, forceful phrasing reaches exceptional eloquence: its harsh tone signals wrath and censure, gathers blame, and exemplifies the Qur’an’s comprehensive expressions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r7.anchor: وهذه الجملة بلغت نهاية الإيجاز وأرفع الجزالة بأسلوب غليظ دال على السخط بالغ حد المذمة ، جامع للملامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r8.claim: The object of “how disbelieving” is omitted because it is obvious: the sense is “how disbelieving he is toward God.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r8.anchor: وحذف المتعلق بلفظ { أكفره } لظهوره من لفظ ( أكفر ) وتقديره : ما أكفره بالله .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r9.claim: The balanced sound of the clause follows the ramal meter in its first, shortened form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#19/r9.anchor: وفي قوله : { قتل الإنسان ما أكفره } محسن الاتزان فإنه من بحر الرمل من عروضه الأولى المحذوفة .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r12.claim: الإنسان is generic in form but specific in intent: the disbeliever.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r12.anchor: قتل الإنسان ما أكفره دعاء على اسم الجنس وهو عموم يراد به الخصوص، والمعنى: قتل الإنسان الكافر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r13.claim: قتل is an imprecation that the disbeliever deserves to be invoked against.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r13.anchor: ومعنى قتل أي هو أهل أن يدعى عليه بهذا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r14.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r14.claim: Mujahid glosses قتل as لعُن, but Ibn Atiyya rejects it as arbitrary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد: قتل بمعنى لعن، وهذا تحكم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r15.claim: ما أكفره may be an exclamation about the extreme degree of disbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r15.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ما أكفره يحتمل معنى التعجب، ويحتمل معنى الاستفهام توقيفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r16.claim: Alternatively, it asks reproachfully: what made him disbelieve?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r16.anchor: ويحتمل معنى الاستفهام توقيفا أي أي شيء أكفره أي جعله كافرا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r17.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r17.claim: The verse reportedly concerns ʿUtba ibn Abi Lahab, who rejected the Lord and was later killed by a lion among his party.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r17.anchor: وقيل إن هذه الآية نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب، وذلك أنه غاضب أباه فأتى النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r18.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r18.claim: The Prophet reportedly prayed God would send His dog against ʿUtba to eat him; another wording asks if he feared God would send it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438/r18.anchor: فيروى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «اللهم ابعث عليه كلبك حتى يأكله»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r1.claim: Qutila means may he be cursed; the human meant here is an unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى قتل الإنسان أي لعن والمراد بالإنسان هاهنا الكافر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid takes the person to mean every unbeliever.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه أشار إلى كل كافر قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies him as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه أمية بن خلف قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r4.claim: Muqātil identifies him as ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r4.anchor: والثالث عتبة بن أبي لهب قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reads the phrase as how intensely he disbelieves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r5.anchor: أحدها ما أشد كفره قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī reads it as what made him disbelieve, a question of rebuke.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r6.anchor: والثاني أي شيء أكفره قاله السدي فعلى هذا يكون استفهام توبيخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes it as an expression of amazement directed at people: marvel at the unbeliever's disbelief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p30#2/r7.anchor: الثالث أنه على وجه التعجب وهذا التعجب يؤمر به الآدميون والمعنى اعجبوا أنتم من كفره قاله الزجاج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r1.claim: The passage condemns the human who denies resurrection, often rejecting it without evidence, through mere improbability and ignorance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى ذاما لمن أنكر البعث والنشور من بني آدم: (قتل الإنسان ما أكفره)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, and Abu Malik gloss qutila al-insan as a curse upon the human being.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: (قتل الإنسان) لعن الإنسان. وكذا قال أبو مالك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir reads the phrase as an exclamation at how intensely the person disbelieves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن جرير (1) (ما أكفره) ما أشد كفره!

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir also allows the question, What made him disbelieve?—that is, what drove him to deny the resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد: أي شيء جعله كافرا؟ أي: ما حمله على التكذيب بالمعاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r5.claim: Qatada, as cited by al-Baghawi from Muqatil and al-Kalbi, takes the phrase to mean how accursed he is.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة-وقد حكاه البغوي عن مقاتل والكلبي-: (ما أكفره) ما ألعنه.

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r3.claim: Mā may be exclamatory (‘How unbelieving he is!’) or interrogative, asking what caused the person’s unbelief.
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r3.anchor: (ما) في قوله: (ما أكفره) يحتمل أن يكون (ما) ابتعجب، ويحتمل معنى، أي،

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r5.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r5.claim: Muqatil reports that the verse was revealed concerning ʿUtba ibn Abi Lahab.
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r5.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (قتل الإنسان ما أكفره) في عتبة بن أبي لهب، عن مقاتل.

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r6.claim: Another report says it concerned the people the Prophet had been calling, mentioned earlier in the sūra.
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r6.anchor: وقيل: فيمن كان يستدعيه النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وهم الذين تقدم ذكرهم في أول السورة.

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r7.claim: Abu Muslim takes ‘the human’ as humanity in general.
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r7.anchor: وقيل: أراد جنس الإنسان، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r8.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r8.claim: Mujahid says no person manages to fulfill everything God has made obligatory.
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد: ما أحد يأتي على جميع ما فرض الله عليه،

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r9.claim: The author prefers that the rebuke targets unbelievers, since it would be impossible to condemn believers in this way.
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r9.anchor: والصحيح أنه في الكفار لاستحالة ذم المؤمنين.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r1.claim: The phrase is a curse against the human being; it is among the harshest because killing is the ultimate worldly hardship and horror.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r1.anchor: دعاء عليه ، وهي من أشنع دعواتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r2.claim: This is an exclamation at the excess of human ingratitude for God’s blessings, expressed with exceptional severity and compression.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r2.anchor: تعجب من إفراطه في كفران نعمة الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r3.claim: The passage traces human life from its beginning, emphasizing abundant blessings and the person’s ingratitude, heedlessness, and failure to give thanks.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r3.anchor: من ابتداء حدوثه ، إلى أن انتهى وما هو مغمور فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r1.claim: Qutila can mean punished or cursed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r1.anchor: في ( قتل ) وجهان : أحدهما : عذب . الثاني : لعن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r2.claim: Al-Insan can refer to every disbeliever.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r2.anchor: أنه إشارة إلى كل كافر , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the person as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r3.anchor: أنه أمية بن خلف , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r4.speaker: ابن جريج والكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r4.claim: They identify him as Utba ibn Abi Lahab, who declared disbelief in the Lord of the setting star; the Prophet prayed against him and a lion killed him on the road to Syria.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r4.anchor: فأخذه الأسد في طريق الشام , قاله ابن جريج والكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r5.claim: On an exclamatory reading, the Arabs’ curse-like expressions show wonder: marvel at how ungrateful the human is after the blessings listed next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r5.anchor: أن ( ما ) تعجب , وعادة العرب إذا تعجبوا من شيء قالوا قاتله الله ما أحسنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r6.speaker: السدي ويحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r6.claim: They read ma as an interrogative: what thing made him disbelieve?
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r6.anchor: أي شيء أكفره , على وجه الاستفهام , قاله السدي ويحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r7.claim: A third interpretation is how accursed he is.

MUQATIL:80:8-17/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r12.claim: Qutila means the human is cursed; the verse refers to the person who disbelieved.
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r12.anchor: يعني لعن الإنسان { مآ أكفره } [آية: 17] يقول: الذي أكفره

MUQATIL:80:8-17/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r13.claim: The verse was revealed concerning ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab: after becoming Muslim during a dispute with his father, he reconciled with him and was sent to Syria for trade, then sent Muhammad word that he had rejected the Star. Muhammad prayed for a beast to devour him, and a lion ate him when he stopped on the road.
MUQATIL:80:8-17/r13.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في عتبة بن أبى لهب بن عبدالمطلب، وذلك أنه كان غضب على أبيه فأتى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فآمن به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r1.claim: The phrase curses the unbelieving human being.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r2.claim: Alternatively, the human being is identified as Umayya or ʿUtba.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r3.claim: The phrase is an interrogative rebuke, asking what has led him to disbelief.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r3.anchor: استفهام توبيخ أى أى شىء جمله على الكفر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r4.claim: Alternatively, it is an exclamation at the intensity of his disbelief.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#15/r4.anchor: أوهو تعجب أى ما أشد كفره

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r1.claim: Qutila here can mean “cursed”; another explanation is “punished.” The human meant is the unbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r1.anchor: «قتل» أي لعن. وقيل: عذب. والإنسان الكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r2.claim: Mujahid says that whenever the Qur'an says “the human was killed/cursed,” it means the unbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r2.anchor: روى الأعمش عن مجاهد قال: ما كان في القرآن «قتل الإنسان» فإنما عني به الكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed about Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, who had believed but renounced the Qur'an after al-Najm, accepting all of it except that surah; the Prophet prayed for a lion to be set on him, and a lion killed him at al-Ghadirah on a Syrian journey despite his companions' precautions. His father had said Muhammad had never spoken falsely.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r3.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب، وكان قد آمن، فلما نزلت «والنجم» ارتد

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r4.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r4.claim: Abu Salih transmits Ibn Abbas's gloss as an exclamation: “How much has he disbelieved!”
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r4.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس «ما أكفره»: أي شيء أكفره؟

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r5.claim: On one account “mā” is exclamative, like Arab curses used to express astonishment; the command is to marvel at the human's disbelief in the blessings described next.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r5.anchor: وقيل: «ما» تعجب وعادة العرب إذا تعجبوا من شيء قالوا: قاتله الله ما أحسنه!

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r6.claim: Another exclamative reading marvels at how much the human disbelieves in God and His blessings despite knowing His abundant kindness.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r6.anchor: وقيل: ما أكفره بالله ونعمه مع معرفته بكثرة إحسانه إليه على التعجب أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the exclamation as “How severe his disbelief is!”
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريح أي ما أشد كفره

QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r8.claim: Alternatively, mā is interrogative: what could have driven him to disbelief? The question rebukes him; mā can be exclamative or interrogative (meaning ayy).
QURTUBI-FULL:80:17-19/r8.anchor: وقيل: «ما» استفهام أي أي شيء دعاه إلى الكفر فهو استفهام توبيخ
